reasoning:
The problem asks for a graph with 30 vertices, at least 42 edges, girth at least 7, and chromatic number at most 5. 
A well-known graph that satisfies these properties is the Tutte-Coxeter graph (also known as the Levi graph of the Cremona-Richmond configuration). 
It is a 3-regular bipartite graph with 30 vertices and 45 edges. 
Because it is bipartite, it is 2-colorable (which is at most 5). 
Its girth is 8 (which is at least 7). 
The number of edges is 45 (which is at least 42). 
We can construct it by taking the 15 pairs of a 6-element set as one part of the bipartition, and the 15 partitions of the set into three pairs as the other part, with edges representing inclusion. This yields the 45 edges provided in the solution.
